      Description
      org.openehealth.ipf.boot.IpfAutoConfiguration.mappingService(SpringMappings)
      as of 6.0, inject SpringMappings instead
      org.openehealth.ipf.commons.audit.BalpAuditContext
      neither of the two properties this used to add is specific to IHE BALP: an audit repository context path belongs to the transport addressing it, and the token claim paths to the token. Both now sit on AuditContext itself, so this interface adds nothing. Use AuditContext.
      org.openehealth.ipf.commons.audit.CustomTlsParameters
      use CustomTlsParameters
      org.openehealth.ipf.commons.audit.DefaultBalpAuditContext
      DefaultAuditContext now carries everything this added. Use it instead.
      org.openehealth.ipf.commons.audit.TlsParameters
      use TlsParameters
      org.openehealth.ipf.commons.core.config.Configurer
      the whole Configurer SPI only ever expressed "collect all beans of type T and push them into some holder", which core Spring expresses as beanFactory.getBeanProvider(T.class).orderedStream(). Holders now collect their own contributions while the singletons are being initialized instead of being filled from the outside once an application context has been refreshed. See org.openehealth.ipf.commons.spring.map.SpringBidiMappingService, org.openehealth.ipf.commons.spring.core.extend.SpringDynamicExtensionRegistrar, org.openehealth.ipf.modules.hl7.config.CustomModelClassesRegistrar and org.openehealth.ipf.platform.camel.core.config.CustomRouteBuilderConfigurer.
      org.openehealth.ipf.commons.core.config.OrderedConfigurer
      see Configurer. Ordering between contributions is now expressed with Spring's @Order / Ordered on the contributing bean itself, which is finer grained than a single order value shared by everything a configurer collected.
      org.openehealth.ipf.commons.core.extend.config.DynamicExtensionConfigurer
      this configurer requires a org.openehealth.ipf.commons.spring.core.config.SpringConfigurationPostProcessor to drive it, and only runs once the application context has been fully refreshed. Declare a org.openehealth.ipf.commons.spring.core.extend.SpringDynamicExtensionRegistrar bean instead, which collects the DynamicExtension beans itself and registers them while the singletons are being initialized. Both mechanisms may be active at the same time; DynamicExtensions.register(DynamicExtension) makes sure that no extension is registered twice.
      org.openehealth.ipf.commons.core.extend.config.DynamicExtensionConfigurer.addExtensionMethods(ExtensionModule)
      use DynamicExtensions.addExtensionMethods(ExtensionModule)
      org.openehealth.ipf.commons.ihe.core.atna.AuditDataset.getW3cTraceContextId()
      the trace context id was never anything but a correlation id read from an HTTP header, which is what AuditDataset.getRequestId() is. Only the participant object it ends up in differs, and that is AuditDataset.getRequestIdType() now.
      org.openehealth.ipf.commons.ihe.core.atna.AuditDataset.setW3cTraceContextId(String)
      use AuditDataset.setRequestId(String, ParticipantObjectIdType), with ParticipantObjectIdTypeCode.W3cTraceContext or, for the Swiss EPR, ParticipantObjectIdTypeCode.SwissW3cTraceContext. This one keeps setting the Swiss code, which is what it always did.
      org.openehealth.ipf.commons.ihe.core.atna.event.IHEAuditMessageBuilder.addSwissW3CTraceContextIdParticipantObject(String)
      use IHEAuditMessageBuilder.addRequestIdParticipantObject(String, ParticipantObjectIdType) with ParticipantObjectIdTypeCode.SwissW3cTraceContext.
      org.openehealth.ipf.commons.ihe.fhir.atna.translation.AuditRecordTranslator(MappingService)
      as of 6.0, pass Mappings instead

      org.openehealth.ipf.commons.map.BidiMappingService
      as of 6.0, use Mappings - DefaultMappings is the implementation to build on, and SpringMappings in ipf-commons-spring the bean to wire. This class remains as an adapter for applications still holding a MappingService, and is scheduled for removal in IPF 7.0.
      org.openehealth.ipf.commons.map.GroovyMappingLoader
      org.openehealth.ipf.commons.map.MappingsBuilder
      org.openehealth.ipf.commons.map.MappingService
      as of 6.0, use Mappings, which is String-typed, returns Optional rather than null, and has neither of the two string conventions this interface's implementations carry. Scheduled for removal in IPF 7.0.
      org.openehealth.ipf.commons.spring.core.config.SpringConfigurationPostProcessor
      the holders and registrars that used to be filled by this listener now collect their own contributions, so this bean can simply be removed from the application context. Running on a ContextRefreshedEvent was also too late: every singleton has been created by then, so anything resolving e.g. a mapping during bean initialization saw an empty MappingService. See SpringBidiMappingService, SpringDynamicExtensionRegistrar, org.openehealth.ipf.modules.hl7.config.CustomModelClassesRegistrar and org.openehealth.ipf.platform.camel.core.config.CustomRouteBuilderConfigurer.

      Note that this listener also created a SpringRegistry as a side effect, and thereby initialized the ContextFacade that the stateful Groovy and Kotlin extensions look up beans in. Contexts that relied on that side effect have to declare the registry explicitly when dropping this bean: 

          <ipf:globalContext/>
      org.openehealth.ipf.commons.spring.map.config.CustomMappingsConfigurer
      SpringMappings -- and the deprecated SpringBidiMappingService where it still owns its mappings -- collects the MappingResourceHolder beans of the application context itself, so this configurer -- and the SpringConfigurationPostProcessor that drives it -- are no longer needed: 
          <bean id="mappings"
          class="org.openehealth.ipf.commons.spring.map.SpringMappings"/>
      Doing so also populates the mappings before the ContextRefreshedEvent instead of after it, once all singletons have been instantiated. Both mechanisms may be active at the same time: SpringMappings.setMappingResource(org.springframework.core.io.Resource, String) ignores resources it has already evaluated.
      org.openehealth.ipf.commons.spring.map.SpringBidiMappingService
      as of 6.0, use SpringMappings and the typed Mappings API. This class remains as an adapter for applications still holding a MappingService, and is scheduled for removal in IPF 7.0.
      org.openehealth.ipf.commons.spring.map.SpringBidiMappingServiceConfigurer
      as of 6.0, along with SpringBidiMappingService. Configure SpringMappings with its mappingResources property, or declare CustomMappings beans, which it collects from the application context by itself.
      org.openehealth.ipf.modules.hl7.config.CustomModelClassFactoryConfigurer
      declare a CustomModelClassesRegistrar instead, which collects the CustomModelClasses beans of the application context itself and therefore needs neither this configurer nor a org.openehealth.ipf.commons.spring.core.config.SpringConfigurationPostProcessor: 
          <bean class="org.openehealth.ipf.modules.hl7.config.CustomModelClassesRegistrar"/>
      The registrar also works in Spring Boot, where custom HL7 model classes could not be contributed through this configurer at all. Both mechanisms may be active at the same time: CustomModelClassesRegistrar.addModels(CustomModelClassFactory, CustomModelClasses, boolean) skips package definitions the factory already knows about.
